jurisdiction.name: Senegal
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Senegal steers AI through its 2023 National AI Strategy and Roadmap and the 2025 New Deal Technologique digital strategy, both of which commit to a national regulatory and ethical framework for AI that has not yet been adopted. Binding rules come only from the 2008 personal data protection law, which limits automated decisions and profiling; the data protection authority (CDP) issued a communiqué on AI and personal data in October 2025. A bill to replace the data protection law is reported to cover AI.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs
Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles (CDP)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on the digital ministry's and the data protection authority's websites. The Official Journal, the National Assembly's and the telecoms regulator's websites could not be accessed. Senegal is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108), but the 2016 law authorising ratification could not be read on an official site, so the convention is not yet linked. The data protection bill and a national data roadmap are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Stratégie nationale et feuille de route du Sénégal sur l'Intelligence Artificielle
instruments.english_title: National Strategy and Roadmap of Senegal on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy (MCTEN)
instruments.current_status: Published by the ministry in 2023 (summary version dated 2023 on its cover); the full 92-page version, titled 'Stratégie de développement de l'intelligence artificielle', is also on mctn.sn (https://api.mctn.sn/fichier/afficher?path=medias%2Fdocuments%2FnOHunv4EKNtWQ8m95RQu1X9jqhf2v9bQDIHNII4Y.pdf). Still cited as the reference AI strategy (SNIA) by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs in September 2026, alongside the 2025 New Deal Technologique.
instruments.summary: Senegal's first national AI strategy (SNIA), developed collaboratively between May and August 2023, sets four fundamental objectives to 2028 and four strategic orientations (human capital; 'from lab to market'; a West African AI hub; trustworthy AI as everyone's business) broken down into about 55 actions in three waves, with a priority roadmap costed at 6.7 billion FCFA over two years. Its governance orientation provides for a national consultation, a balanced and flexible AI regulation based on risk categorisation, an AI regulation guide, a pre-figuration body for a future AI regulator, regulatory sandboxes, mandatory impact assessments for some AI uses and ethical criteria in public procurement specifications, with a governance framework to be in place by the end of 2026.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy and the main source of Senegal's planned AI governance and regulatory framework.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs

instruments.english_title: Technological New Deal – Horizon 2034 (national digital strategy)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs (MCTN), launched by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Launched 24 February 2025 by the President of the Republic; implementation through priority programmes was under way in 2026 (e.g. launch of structuring projects on 24 March 2026). The PDF linked from the ministry's own 'Télécharger le New Deal Technologique' documentation entry is a placeholder file, so the strategy's dedicated site is the official copy.
instruments.summary: Senegal's national digital strategy to 2034, launched on 24 February 2025 within the Vision Sénégal 2050 national transformation agenda and succeeding the Sénégal Numérique 2025 strategy. It is organised in four axes (digital sovereignty, digitalisation of public services, development of the digital economy, African digital leadership) implemented through a Digital Master Plan. Its strategic objective OS-3.3 on artificial intelligence commits to establishing a national regulatory and ethical framework for AI ensuring transparency, data protection and digital sovereignty, alongside AI infrastructure (data centres, supercomputing) and AI use in public administration.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current government digital strategy with an explicit AI pillar and a commitment to a national AI regulatory and ethical framework.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 2008-12 du 25 janvier 2008 portant sur la Protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Senegal (law promulgated by the President of the Republic)
instruments.current_status: In force; implemented by Decree 2008-721 of 30 June 2008. A revision bill to replace it (reported to address AI, biometrics and big data and to replace the CDP with a new authority) has not been adopted as of October 2026; held as a lead.
instruments.summary: Senegal's general data protection law, which applies to automated and non-automated processing of personal data and creates the Personal Data Protection Commission (CDP) as an independent administrative authority. Article 48 prohibits court decisions involving an assessment of a person's behaviour from being based on automated processing intended to evaluate aspects of their personality, and bars any decision with legal effects from being taken solely on the basis of automated processing intended to profile the person, with limited contract-related exceptions. Automated processing on behalf of the State in sensitive areas requires a regulatory act after a reasoned CDP opinion (article 21).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling that govern AI systems processing personal data; a revision bill covering AI and biometrics is pending (see leads).
metadata_gaps: effective_date: not stated in the text read (Official Journal publication reference not available)

instruments.official_title: Communiqué sur l'usage de l'intelligence artificielle et la protection des données personnelles
instruments.english_title: Communiqué on the Use of Artificial Intelligence and the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.current_status: Published on the CDP website on 8 October 2025 as a formal stamped communiqué.
instruments.summary: Statement by the data protection authority responding to AI-generated videos and images of public figures, religious leaders and citizens circulating on social media, which it says can seriously harm human dignity and expose their authors to sanctions. It lists the risks of irresponsible AI use (mass collection of personal data without people's knowledge, identity theft and reputational harm, deceptive deepfakes) and calls for ethical use of AI systems, urging citizens to be vigilant, content creators to refrain from harmful manipulation and platforms to strengthen detection and reporting of illicit content.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The data protection regulator's only AI-specific public guidance found; addresses generative AI and deepfakes.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): two-page stamped PDF read (rendered as images, read visually); date 8 October 2025 taken from the CDP site's communiqué/news listing, as the PDF itself is undated

organizations.name: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for digital policy (MCTN; called Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy (MCTEN) when the 2023 AI strategy was drafted, and presenting itself as Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs in 2026 publications). Steered the 2023 national AI strategy and the 2025 New Deal Technologique digital strategy, and in 2026 led the national data-valorisation Blueprint covering data and AI use cases.

organizations.name: Personal Data Protection Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Commission de Protection des Données Personnelles (CDP), independent administrative authority created by Law 2008-12; supervises personal data processing, including automated decision-making limits, and issued an October 2025 communiqué on AI use and deepfakes.
